title: Patchbay — Modular Synth Rack
description: Drag eleven kinds of module onto a rack, patch them with coloured cables, and record the result to a WAV file.
concept: A semi-modular synthesizer that works the way hardware does: every module exposes jacks, and nothing makes a sound until you run a cable from one to another. Audio, CV and gate are three separate signal types with three cable colours, and the rack refuses a patch whose colours disagree — so the routing teaches itself. A 16-step sequencer drives envelopes over gate cables and oscillators over a v/oct line, and the master bus is tapped so any patch can be recorded and downloaded as real audio.
features: Eleven module types — oscillator, noise, LFO, filter, ADSR, VCA, drive, delay, reverb, 16-step sequencer and output
Type-checked cable patching: click an output jack then an input jack; click a cable to cut it
16-step sequencer with per-step pitch by vertical drag, glide, gate length, octave shift and randomise
Four built-in patches (Acid Line, Dub Chord Stab, Wobble Bass, Hiss Drone) that load and start playing
Record the master bus and export a 16-bit WAV download
Save the patch as JSON, share it as a URL hash, and autosave to localStorage
Live oscilloscope and spectrum on the master output

interaction.mouse: Drag module headers to rearrange the rack; drag sliders to shape each module; drag a step vertically to set its pitch.
interaction.click: Click an output jack then a matching input jack to patch; click a cable to cut it; double-click a jack to unpatch it.
interaction.touch: Everything is pointer-driven — tap to patch, drag to move and edit steps; the module rail scrolls horizontally.
interaction.keyboard: Space toggles the transport, R starts and stops recording, Escape cancels a half-made patch.
